gap: No result ChatGPT got states OutdoorGearLab's lab measurements of the ~1 kWh units side by side. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 gave 910 Wh of usable AC and weighed 24.4 lb on their scale, against 23.8 lb claimed. That is the most usable energy per pound of the group at 37.3 Wh/lb. But it recharged at only 563 Wh/hr, about 1.9 h, while the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 recharged at 1,097 Wh/hr (890 Wh, 25.2 lb), the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 gave 890 Wh at 25.0 lb, and the EcoFlow DELTA 3 gave 870 Wh at 28.1 lb.
standout_why: I opened backup-power.org/best-1000wh-power-stations (cited). It says 'We don't test products in a lab' and gives only maker specs plus a calculated 870–980 Wh usable estimate. I opened thepowerstationguide.com/blog/best-1000wh-portable-power-stations (cited). It says 'All figures are manufacturer claims' and gives an 800–850 Wh usable estimate. ChatGPT's own answer says 'Weights are published specifications, not independently verified measurements.' I could not open enoughwatts.com or unpluggedwatts.com (TLS certificate error), so I can't confirm that those two lack measurements. None of the pages I read has a measured usable-Wh figure, a scale weight or a measured recharge rate from a named tester.
decides: Weight and size were the shopper's own deciding factors, and the measurements settle them. The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 stays the pick. In OutdoorGearLab's test it delivered the most usable energy of the 1 kWh units (910 Wh) and was still the lightest on the scale (24.4 lb). The measurements also add something the spec tables hide: on a default wall charge it is the slowest to refill except the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (563 Wh/hr against 1,097 for the Anker and 1,229 for the DELTA 3). nextpit did reach a full charge in about 50 minutes using Jackery's app-enabled emergency mode. Anyone who refills between outages should pick the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, accepting that OutdoorGearLab called its fan loud and Notebookcheck measured 45 dB at 1 m. The BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 is the quiet choice (OutdoorGearLab: fan 'remarkably quiet' at 80% load), with the same 890 Wh as the Anker but slower charging (512 Wh/hr).
